contexts.text: The good of love is the threshing-floor () from the grain and the derivative bread there. AE 376:17.

They came to the threshing-floor Atad () = the first state; for a threshing-floor = where there is the good of truth; for there is grain in a threshing-floor, and by grain is signified the good which is from truth, and also the truth of good.
Not a face, but only the broad area of one...
In safety, or within the area.
The threshing-floor () = where the separation is effected.
The threshing-floor () = the doctrine of the Church.

Upon all the corn floors () = all things of the Word and of doctrine from the Word; for corn, from which is bread, = all that which spiritually nourishes, and threshing-floor = where it is collected together, thus the Word. The threshing-floor and the press shall not feed them = that they will not draw from the Word the goods of charity and of love, thus not anything which will nourish the soul; for the threshing-floor, here, = the Word as to the goods of charity; and the press, as to the goods of love: by the press, here, is meant oil...
The produce of the threshing-floor () = all the good of the Church; the same as bread, and corn.
